items.title: v2.1.195
items.bullet_md: - 🛠 **[v2.1.195](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.195)** — _Claude Code releases_. — v2.1.195 switches hyphenated hook matchers from substring to exact matching — `mcp__brave-search` no longer over-matches unrelated tool names — and fixes background jobs showing a blank screen for up to 5s on restart. Adds `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS` to keep scroll while suppressing click/drag/hover in fullscreen.

score_components.taste_reason: Actionable Claude Code release with a new env var for fullscreen users plus two real bugfixes; extends state-of-ai's v2.1.157 row.

items.title: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol: a next-generation model
items.bullet_md: - 🟢 **[Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol: a next-generation model](https://openai.com/index/previewing-gpt-5-6-sol)** — _OpenAI blog_. — OpenAI announced GPT-5.6 Sol alongside two cheaper models — Terra matches GPT-5.5 for roughly half the price — but restricted the preview to government-approved partners after a White House request, one of the first concrete effects of this month's AI executive order.

score_components.taste_reason: New GPT-5.6 Sol model announcement from OpenAI extends state-of-ai's Frontier row beyond GPT-5.5; hot-drop worthy of Slacking to a coworker even though the preview body is light on specifics.

items.title: Our latest Google Finance upgrades, including a new app
items.bullet_md: - 🔵 **[Our latest Google Finance upgrades, including a new app](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/google-finance-updates-june-2026/)** — _Google AI blog_. — After 20 years as a web-only service, Google Finance gets a dedicated Android app and brings back portfolio tracking — removed in 2017 — now powered by Gemini AI to analyze holdings and generate market briefings.

score_components.taste_reason: Google Finance app update is off-topic — not AI news, pure product marketing for a non-AI feature.

items.title: Ornith (35B,9B) + Hermes,Zed: THE FULLY PRIVATE LOCAL AGENT is ACTUALLY HERE!
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Ornith (35B,9B) + Hermes,Zed: THE FULLY PRIVATE LOCAL AGENT is ACTUALLY HERE!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9PkNh6b1P8A) — **AICodeKing** (6m07s). — Run Ornith-1.0 models locally with Hermes Agent and Zed — DeepReinforce's MIT-licensed coding family from 9B to 397B achieves 82.4% on SWE-Bench Verified, matching Opus 4.7 without sending code to an API.

score_components.taste_reason: New Ornith open model family (9B-397B) for local agentic coding is genuinely relevant to the audience, but all-caps clickbait title and YouTube-summary source reduce credibility.

items.title: AI News: The New Model That's As Good As Fable
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [AI News: The New Model That's As Good As Fable](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zMVZvgCOr40) — **Matt Wolfe** (20m01s). — Sakana's Fugu orchestrates GPT-5.5, Opus 4.8, and Gemini 3.1 Pro through one API, scoring 73.7 on SWE-Bench Pro — worth watching if export controls have you rethinking your model stack.

score_components.taste_reason: Sakana AI matching Fable on some benchmarks is modestly interesting but the roundup format from Matt Wolfe lacks specific numbers to anchor; title slightly oversells.

items.title: I Built a Business That Makes €10K/Month With Claude Code (Full System)

score_components.taste_reason: Clickbait business case-study title from a small YouTube channel; not technical, no novel AI insight for the senior engineer audience.

items.title: The government's AI kill switch has a blind spot
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [The government's AI kill switch has a blind spot](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y9nJoLtIpsc) — **Roske AI** (2m57s). — Useful for anyone tracking whether government regulation can meaningfully constrain frontier AI — the 2m57s argument contrasts the overnight shutdown of Anthropic's Fable 5 against the staggered rollout of GPT-5.6, noting that open-weight models evade both.

score_components.taste_reason: Valid but well-trodden point about open-weights creating a regulatory blind spot from a 3-minute unknown YouTube channel; no new facts or reporting.

items.title: Can a Free Local LLM Actually Replace Claude Code or Codex ?
items.bullet_md: - 🎥 [Can a Free Local LLM Actually Replace Claude Code or Codex ?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3uOOwUCfl9w) — **Cloud Codes** (9m48s). — A benchmark-style comparison testing whether free local LLMs can keep up with Claude Code and Codex on real programming tasks — for developers weighing the cost savings of local inference against cloud-grade agent capability.

score_components.taste_reason: Broad local-vs-cloud comparison with no specific model or benchmark named; audience already runs Claude Code daily and knows the tradeoffs.

score_components.taste_reason: GLM-5.2 demo in OpenCode from AICodeKing; same model as the AlphaSignal piece but with less concrete data and more clickbait framing.

items.title: LLM Performance on a Real, Double-Marked GCSE Benchmark
items.bullet_md: - 🧪 **[LLM Performance on a Real, Double-Marked GCSE Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24973)** — _arXiv cs.CL_. — A new benchmark of 32,534 double-marked GCSE responses finds that top LLMs agree with examiners more closely than two examiners agree with each other, including on handwritten maths and English essays.

score_components.taste_reason: LLM-vs-human-examiner agreement study on 32K GCSE responses; interesting evaluation dataset but niche educational benchmarking.
